title: Configure a Small Office LAN
realWorldScenario: A small office with two employees needs a basic network. Both PCs must be able to communicate with each other and share a printer. The network administrator has assigned the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet for this office.
problemStatement: The two office PCs are physically connected to SW1 but cannot communicate because they have no IP addresses configured.
businessImpact: Employees cannot share files, access shared resources, or print to the network printer. This impacts office productivity.
objectives: Configure IPv4 addressing on two PCs, verify layer 2 connectivity through the switch, and test end-to-end connectivity using ping.
learningObjectives: Understand the relationship between IP addresses and network connectivity
Configure IPv4 addresses on end devices
Understand how switches forward frames based on MAC addresses
prerequisites: Basic understanding of IP addressing (network vs host portions)
concepts: IPv4 address structure and dotted-decimal notation
Subnet mask and its role in determining the network
skills: Configure IP address on a PC
Use the ping command for connectivity testing

steps.title: Verify Initial Connectivity
steps.instruction: Before configuring any IP addresses, try to ping PC2 from PC1 to see the current state. Open PC1's command prompt and run: ping 192.168.1.20
steps.why: Establishes a baseline. You should see 'Request timed out' because PC1 has no IP address yet.
steps.expectedOutput: Request timed out (because PC1 has no IP address)
hints: PC1 needs an IP address before it can communicate
Use 'ipconfig' to check current IP configuration

commonMistakes.solution: Assign an IP address first, then test connectivity

steps.completionCondition: Student runs ping and sees request timed out
steps.optionalConcept: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is used for error reporting and diagnostics

steps.title: Configure IP Address on PC1
steps.instruction: Configure PC1 with IP address 192.168.1.10 and subnet mask 255.255.255.0. On the simulation interface, set the IP address to: 192.168.1.10/24
steps.why: PC1 needs an IP address to participate in the network. The subnet mask 255.255.255.0 (/24) tells PC1 that addresses 192.168.1.1 through 192.168.1.254 are on the same local network.
hints: In a real PC, you would go to Network Settings > IPv4 Properties
The /24 notation means the first 24 bits are network, leaving 8 bits for hosts (254 usable addresses)

commonMistakes.mistake: Using an IP address already assigned to another device
commonMistakes.solution: Each device must have a unique IP address on the same network

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a subnet mask that doesn't match PC2's mask
commonMistakes.solution: All devices on the same subnet must use the same subnet mask

steps.title: Configure IP Address on PC2
steps.instruction: Configure PC2 with IP address 192.168.1.20 and subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Use the same subnet mask as PC1.
steps.why: PC2 also needs an IP address to participate. Using .20 gives it a unique address in the same 192.168.1.0/24 network as PC1.
hints: Both PCs should use the same subnet mask (255.255.255.0) to be on the same network

commonMistakes.mistake: Configuring PC2 with a different subnet mask
commonMistakes.solution: All devices in the same network segment must use the same subnet mask

steps.title: Verify IP Configuration
steps.instruction: On PC1, run 'ipconfig' to verify the IP address and subnet mask are correctly configured.
steps.why: Always verify your configuration before testing connectivity. This confirms PC1 has the correct addressing.
hints: The ipconfig command shows the current TCP/IP configuration on Windows

steps.title: Test Connectivity with Ping
steps.instruction: From PC1, ping PC2 at 192.168.1.20 to verify they can communicate.
steps.why: Ping is the most basic connectivity test. It uses ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages to verify that packets can reach the destination and get back.
steps.expectedOutput:
Reply from 192.168.1.20: bytes=32 time<1ms TTL=128

Packets: Sent = 4, Received = 4, Lost = 0 (0% loss)
hints: A successful ping shows 'Reply from' - this means the packet reached PC2 and PC2 sent a reply
Failed ping shows 'Request timed out' - meaning the packet didn't reach or no reply came back

commonMistakes.solution: Check: 1) Are both PCs on the same subnet? 2) Is the cable connected? 3) Are the interfaces up?

steps.title: Verify Reverse Connectivity
steps.instruction: From PC2, ping PC1 at 192.168.1.10 to verify bidirectional connectivity.
steps.why: Network connectivity should be symmetrical. Testing in both directions confirms both devices can send and receive.
hints: If PC1 can ping PC2 but PC2 cannot ping PC1, check PC1's firewall settings

troubleshootingSteps: 1. Verify PC1 has an IP address (ipconfig)
2. Verify PC2 has an IP address (ipconfig)
3. Check both IPs are in the same subnet (192.168.1.x)
5. Check switch ports are not disabled
commonErrors.fix: Configure IP addresses on both PCs, verify cable connections
commonErrors.verificationAfterFix: Run ping again - should see replies

finalVerification.successCriteria: Both PCs have correct IP addresses, are on the same subnet, and can ping each other successfully.
finalVerification.completionCriteria: Student has configured both PCs with correct IPs and verified bidirectional connectivity.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the purpose of a subnet mask?
options: To determine which part of an IP address is the network and which is the host
knowledgeCheck.correctAnswer: To determine which part of an IP address is the network and which is the host
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The subnet mask tells devices which IP addresses are on the local network (same broadcast domain) and which require a router to reach.

knowledgeCheck.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /24 network?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: A /24 network has 256 total addresses (192.168.1.0 - 192.168.1.255), but .0 is the network address and .255 is the broadcast address, leaving 254 usable host addresses.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does the ping command use?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Ping uses ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) Echo Request and Echo Reply messages to test connectivity.
